what_it_measured.text: ABSTRACT: The main aim of this study was to evaluate the in vitro and in vivo eﬃciency of the polyaspartic acid- and acrylic acid-based superabsorbent polymer.
The main objective of synthesizing superabsorbent polymer was to use a polymer with moistureretaining capacity.

route.text: After creating the burn wound, the polymeric materials were applied on the wound bed.42

endpoint.text: The blood compatibility of the polymeric material has been evaluated by studying the blood clotting and protein adsorption test.
Furthermore, the release mechanism was evaluated using four models, viz., zero-order, ﬁrst-order, Korsmeyer Peppas, and Higuchi.

reported_results.text: The EGDMA-based polymer with 1:1 ratio (PASP:AA) was further evaluated on animal models (in vivo studies) as this polymer showed good peptide release eﬃciency. 2.2.
The encapsulation eﬃciency of the polymer/monomer ratio 1:1 with EGDMA as cross-linker has been found to be 78.36%.
A 25−50% improvement in concentration levels was observed with polymer with GHK-Cu on 15th day (Table 4).
